Deployment 1: Human-in-the-loop review of the conductivity and salinity data have identified this deployment as impacted by a salinity drift issue. This issue appears as an initial low-salinity offset followed by a quasi-exponential drift back to a stable value as described in OOI Document 3408-30001 as well as Sea-Bird Application Note 97. Conductivity and salinity data impacted by this issue should either be discarded or corrected following the methods outlined in OOI Document 3408-30001. An example correction can be found at https://github.com/WHOIGit/ooicgsn-data-tools/tree/master/WFP_Salinity_Drift. Computed oxygen concentration, but not raw oxygen data, is also impacted.

To receive instant notification of updates to the code, add yourself as a watcher to the GitHub repository linked above. For further questions please email help@oceanobservatories.org.

Deployment 1: Human-in-the-loop review of the conductivity and salinity data have identified this deployment as impacted by a salinity drift issue. This issue appears as an initial low-salinity offset followed by a quasi-exponential drift back to a stable value as described in OOI Document 3408-30001 as well as Sea-Bird Application Note 97. Conductivity and salinity data impacted by this issue should either be discarded or corrected following the methods outlined in OOI Document 3408-30001. An example correction can be found at https://github.com/WHOIGit/ooicgsn-data-tools/tree/master/WFP_Salinity_Drift. Computed oxygen concentration, but not raw oxygen data, is also impacted.

Deployment 1: Due to delays on deck during deployment, the profiler's first dive began before the anchor was dropped. Once the dive started, the winch roller engaged and the profiler began its descent, which in this case meant winching back toward the boat/anchor. This may have damaged the winch mechanism or started the profiler into a non-standard deployment mode. The upper profiler (WFP02) indicated an error condition upon recovery, and a large number of profiles failed to log any CTD data. The lower profiler's battery voltage dropped rapidly near profile 300, which appears to have slowed down the profiling speed and increased the profile duration.

CE02SHSP-00006 reported that it had surfaced unexpectedly April 25 at 5:10 pm local time. Within a few hours it was determined that it was still tethered to its anchor. It's beacon wasn't reporting either. The profiler and its anchor were recovered the following day. Data were sent to the profiler vendor. By April 28 we confirmed there was a firmware bug that had never been seen before. While moving between two positions, the control canister thought the profiler was 20 cm below its destination, but the profiler's winch thought the profiler was 20 cm above its destination, so the profiler was winched up to the surface, instead of retreating 20 cm to its parking depth. The bug will be corrected in the next firmware release. It also turns out that the beacon was programmed improperly, so it had run out of batteries. We switched to a new beacon model this year and confirmed with the vendor which settings to use.

Due to a calibration error, this instrument reported oxygen levels that could be as much as 4.2 percent too low. Statement from the manufacturer: A recent routine control check of the O2 reference sensors, used for multipoint calibration of oxygen Optodes, revealed a deviation with respect to accuracy. The revealed deviation in the reference sensors is a 2.7 percent linear loss (percent of reading) in response to oxygen which means that these optodes will report oxygen levels that could be as much as 4.2 percent too low (deviation in slope). The 2.7 percent deviation is in excess of the specified MPC accuracy of +/-1.5 percent.

Deployment 5: Human-in-the-loop review of the conductivity and salinity data have identified this deployment as impacted by a salinity drift issue. This issue appears as an initial low-salinity offset followed by a quasi-exponential drift back to a stable value as described in OOI Document 3408-30001 as well as Sea-Bird Application Note 97. Conductivity and salinity data impacted by this issue should either be discarded or corrected following the methods outlined in OOI Document 3408-30001. An example correction can be found at https://github.com/WHOIGit/ooicgsn-data-tools/tree/master/WFP_Salinity_Drift. Computed oxygen concentration, but not raw oxygen data, is also impacted.

Deployment 6: Human-in-the-loop review of the conductivity and salinity data have identified this deployment as impacted by a salinity drift issue. This issue appears as an initial low-salinity offset followed by a quasi-exponential drift back to a stable value as described in OOI Document 3408-30001 as well as Sea-Bird Application Note 97. Conductivity and salinity data impacted by this issue should either be discarded or corrected following the methods outlined in OOI Document 3408-30001. An example correction can be found at https://github.com/WHOIGit/ooicgsn-data-tools/tree/master/WFP_Salinity_Drift. Computed oxygen concentration, but not raw oxygen data, is also impacted.

Deployment 6: Human-in-the-loop review of the conductivity and salinity data have identified this deployment as impacted by a salinity drift issue. This issue appears as an initial low-salinity offset followed by a quasi-exponential drift back to a stable value as described in OOI Document 3408-30001 as well as Sea-Bird Application Note 97. Conductivity and salinity data impacted by this issue should either be discarded or corrected following the methods outlined in OOI Document 3408-30001. An example correction can be found at https://github.com/WHOIGit/ooicgsn-data-tools/tree/master/WFP_Salinity_Drift. Computed oxygen concentration, but not raw oxygen data, is also impacted.

Deployment 2: This glider was deployed with a slightly modified optode to improve calibration by exposing it to air. The optode mount was moved to a spot slightly forward of the glider's fin and oriented so that the optode would be above the waterline when the glider was at the surface. The optode remains powered and logging during the air surface intervals after finishing a dive. Additionally, all sensors were changed from descent-only to ascent-only logging to avoid sensor lag artifacts when moving from air to water.

*UPDATE 2025-08-12: Through internal validation and user input, Sea-Bird Scientific discovered all CDOM sensors calibrated prior to 2023 were affected by improperly prepared primary standards. Sea-Bird provided corrected scale factors for all relevant calibration events and new coefficients have been entered into the OOI system as of July 2025. All derived L1 and L2 data products generated prior to this date should be re-requested in order to ensure utilization of the correct calibration values.* Sea-Bird Scientific issued a notification that some CDOM fluorometers were producing biased values, which was traced back to three distinct root causes: Incorrect primary CDOM standard, in situ bias, and out-of-tolerance UV LEDs. We are working with Sea-Bird to obtain correction factors for the affected instruments; in the meantime, the CDOM data should be considered suspect and should not be used in any analyses

*UPDATE 2025-08-12: Through internal validation and user input, Sea-Bird Scientific discovered all CDOM sensors calibrated prior to 2023 were affected by improperly prepared primary standards. Sea-Bird provided corrected scale factors for all relevant calibration events and new coefficients have been entered into the OOI system as of July 2025. All derived L1 and L2 data products generated prior to this date should be re-requested in order to ensure utilization of the correct calibration values.* Sea-Bird Scientific issued a notification that some CDOM fluorometers were producing biased values, which was traced back to three distinct root causes: Incorrect primary CDOM standard, in situ bias, and out-of-tolerance UV LEDs. We are working with Sea-Bird to obtain correction factors for the affected instruments; in the meantime, the CDOM data should be considered suspect and should not be used in any analyses

Deployment 7: Human-in-the-loop review of the conductivity and salinity data have identified this deployment as impacted by a salinity drift issue. This issue appears as an initial low-salinity offset followed by a quasi-exponential drift back to a stable value as described in OOI Document 3408-30001 as well as Sea-Bird Application Note 97. Conductivity and salinity data impacted by this issue should either be discarded or corrected following the methods outlined in OOI Document 3408-30001. An example correction can be found at https://github.com/WHOIGit/ooicgsn-data-tools/tree/master/WFP_Salinity_Drift. Computed oxygen concentration, but not raw oxygen data, is also impacted.

Deployments: 7,8, & 9; The CDOM and Backscatter (bb) calibration coefficients were switched and the OOINet and raw data are wrong.  These can be corrected by recalculating the L1 data from the L0 data ("sci_flbbcd_*_sig" variables) using the algorithm `L1 = (L0 - dc) * sf`; where dc is "dark_counts" and sf is "scale_factor". For this deployment cdom: dc=52, sf=0.0839 ; backscatter/bb: dc=43, sf=2.345E-06 and then use function flo_back_total (https://tinyurl.com/mendyzb4) to convert from L1 to L2.

Conductivity and salinity data impacted by this issue should either be discarded or corrected following the methods outlined in OOI Document 3408-30001. An example correction can be found at https://github.com/WHOIGit/ooicgsn-data-tools/tree/master/WFP_Salinity_Drift. Computed oxygen concentration, but not raw oxygen data, is also impacted.

These can be corrected by recalculating the L1 data from the L0 "sci_bsipar_sensor_volts" variable in the recovered data set using the algorithm `L1 = (L0 - sd) / sf`; where sd is the "sensor_dark" and "sf" is the wet scale_factor calibration parameters. For this deployment, sd=0.0098 Volts and sf=5.949E-4

Deployment: 00012; The incorrect Chlorophyll, CDOM, and Backscatter (bb) calibrations were on the glider so the OOINet and raw data is wrong. These can be corrected by recalculating the L1 data from the L0 data (the "sci_flbbcd_*_sig" variables) using the algorithm `L1 = (L0 - dc) * sf`; where dc is "dark_counts" and "sf" is scale_factor. For this deployment, chlor: dc=50, sf=0.0068; cdom: dc=48, sf=0.1039 ; backscatter/bb: dc =46, sf=2.131E-06 and then use function flo_back_total (https://tinyurl.com/mendyzb4) to convert from L1 to L2.

Deployment 00004: The fluorometer instrument had the incorrect calibration values on board the glider for the first 33 hours before being corrected. This affects the Chlorophyll, CDOM, and Backscatter data.  The first 33 hours can be corrected by using the dark count and scale factor calibration coefficients for each measurement and applying the algorithm `value = sf * (signal - dc)` where signal is the raw counts signal from each sensor, and dc and sf are the dark counts and scale factor from the calibration certificate documents for the instrument.

Deployment 00004: The PAR instrument had the incorrect calibration values on board the glider for the first 33 hours before being corrected. The first 33 hours can be corrected by using the dark count and scale factor calibration coefficients from the calibration certificate by applying the algorithm `value = (sensor_volts - dc)/sf` where sensor_volts is the raw sensor voltage measurement and dc and sf are the dark counts and scale factor from the calibration certificate document for the instrument.

This sensor was calibrated after 2023 and NOT impacted by the calibration correction.* Sea-Bird Scientific issued a notification that some CDOM fluorometers were producing biased values, which was traced back to three distinct root causes: Incorrect primary CDOM standard, in situ bias, and out-of-tolerance UV LEDs.
